identity.title: Towards sub-kpc scale kinematics of molecular and ionized gas of star-forming galaxies at z ∼ 1

paper_type_evidence.quote: We have presented the molecular gas kinematics from ALMA CO(4-3) observations of two highly magnified galaxies at $z~\sim~1$ and compared it with the $[$O II$]$  kinematics obtained with MUSE/VLT

evidence.quote: located behind the clusters MACSJ1206.2-0847 and Abell 0521, respectively.
located behind the clusters MACSJ1206.2-0847 and Abell 0521, respectively.

question.value: Do molecular (CO) and ionized ([O II]) gas rotation curves and velocity dispersions differ in two lensed z~1 galaxies, and can disk geometry (radius, thickness) explain it?

evidence.loc: 7 Analysis of two lensed z~1 galaxies
evidence.quote: we investigate if the difference observed between the rotation curves and velocity dispersion values of the molecular and ionized gas can be explained by geometrical effects in the Cosmic Snake and A521.
Observations of the Cosmic Snake were carried out in Cycle 3 (project 2013.1.01330.S)
A521 was observed in Cycle 4 (project 2016.1.00643.S) using the C40-6 configuration
The total on-source integration time was of 52.3 minutes in band 6.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: CO(4-3) at 226.44 GHz (Snake) and 225.66 GHz (A521); channel 7.8125 MHz (~10.3 km/s)

evidence.quote: The spectral resolution was tuned to 7.8125 MHz ($\rm \sim 10.3\, km \, s^{-1}$) for both galaxies.
We observed the CO(4-3) emission line at the observed frequency of 226.44 GHz which corresponds to a redshift of $z=1.036$.

configurations.value: Snake: C38-5 (max baseline 1.6 km, 38 antennae); A521: C40-6 (max baseline 3.1 km, 41 antennae)

evidence.quote: performed in the extended C38-5 configuration with the maximum baseline of 1.6 km and 38 of the 12 meters antennae
The final synthesized beam size is $0.22'' \times 0.18''$ with a position angle of +85$^\circ$ for the Cosmic Snake and $0.20'' \times 0.17''$ at $-71^\circ$ for A521.

analysis_steps.goal: Match resolution and make moment maps

method.value: Smooth to MUSE PSF with imsmooth, then immoments for velocity and dispersion with 3 sigma threshold

evidence.quote: with a 3$\sigma$ threshold parameter above the noise level applied when producing the first (velocity) and second (velocity dispersion) moment maps

analysis_steps.goal: Extract rotation curves and dispersion profiles

method.value: Source-plane annuli projected to image plane; major axis from steepest gradient; apertures of PSF size along major axis; average positive sides of two counter-images

evidence.quote: The rotation curves and velocity dispersion profiles have been measured directly from the velocity and velocity dispersion maps in the image plane by taking an aperture corresponding to the PSF along the major axis.

validation.value: Verified with simulated galaxy in source plane projected to image plane; kinematics recovered within 10%

evidence.quote: We accurately recovered the kinematics (with an error less than 10%).

method.value: Measure dispersion along major axis at radii larger than R_e where curve is flat; correct for instrumental broadening in quadrature

evidence.quote: We determine the intrinsic velocity dispersion by directly measuring the velocity dispersion maps along the major axis in the outer regions

validation.value: Compared with Patricio2018 values from a different method

evidence.quote: (cite: Patricio2018) used a different method to estimate the intrinsic velocity dispersion

analysis_steps.goal: Model rotation curves with particle disks

method.value: Stellar and gas Miyamoto-Nagai disks of particles in equilibrium; project at inclination, average LOS velocities, smooth to observed resolution, extract along major axis; vary R_gas, H_gas and resolution H*tan(i)

evidence.quote: we assume an inclination and then produce a 2D velocity map by taking the average velocity of the particles along the line of sight in each spatial element.

findings_qualitative.value: Snake CO rotation curve is steeper than [O II]; A521 curves agree at ~2-3 kpc resolution

evidence.quote: The molecular gas curve is steeper and reaches the maximum rotation velocity at a smaller radius from the center than the ionized gas curve.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular and ionized gas rotation curves differ at sub-kpc resolution
claims.experiment: Compare CO(4-3) ALMA and [O II] MUSE rotation curves of the lensed Snake and A521
claims.result: Snake CO curve steeper in inner 0-2 kpc; A521 curves agree at few-kpc resolution
claims.finding: Differences appear when resolution is sufficient

evidence.quote: In A521, the molecular and ionized gas rotation curves agree, but the spatial resolution is only of a few kpc on the major axis.

claims.experiment: Particle simulations of stellar plus two gas disks
claims.result: Different radii and heights reproduce the Snake curves; H_ion~1 kpc
claims.finding: Molecular disk is more concentrated and thinner than the ionized disk

evidence.quote: The rotation curves of the molecular and ionized gas are well reproduced by disks with different radii and heights.

claims.finding: A521 ionized gas may be a thick turbulent disk

evidence.quote: This difference could indicate the presence of a thick and turbulent ionized gas disk.

why_this_data.value: Lensing gives a few hundred pc resolution for comparing tracers

evidence.quote: we can compare the molecular and ionized gas kinematics of these two galaxies at high spatial resolution (a few hundred parsecs on average).

limitations_admitted.value: A521 lacks resolution along the major axis, so differences may be hidden

evidence.quote: The lack of spatial resolution can easily prevent to see a difference between two rotation curves.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only two galaxies; no formal fit or uncertainties for the simulation comparison
Model parameters partly tuned (H_ion), not fitted
Lens model uncertainty propagates to radii
